title: Buddha Avatar (Storybook): The Prince Who Woke Up
label: BUDDHA  ·  THE NINTH AVATAR
sources: Traditional life of the Buddha (Buddhacarita of Ashvaghosha; Nidanakatha): birth at Lumbini, Asita's prophecy, the four sights, the great departure, six years of austerity, Sujata's offering, Mara, awakening under the Bodhi tree, forty-five years of teaching
Bhagavata Purana 1.3.24 and Gita Govinda (Dashavatara stotra) for the Buddha among the avatars of Vishnu

lines.text: Long ago, in a garden called Lumbini, a prince was born, named Siddhartha.
lines.say: Long ago, in a garden called Loombinee, a prince was born, named Sid-dartha.

lines.text: A wise man foretold, he would become a great king, or a great teacher.
His father wanted a king, so he hid every sorrow behind the palace walls.
Siddhartha grew up among music, gardens, and endless spring.
lines.say: Sid-dartha grew up among music, gardens, and endless spring.

lines.text: But one day, he rode out beyond the gates.
He saw an old man, bent with age. A sick man, shaking with fever.
And a silent procession, carrying someone who would never wake.
Then he saw a wandering monk, who owned nothing, and yet was at peace.
That night, he looked once at his sleeping wife and son, and quietly left the palace.
He cut off his long hair, and traded his silks for a simple robe.
For six years he searched, fasting until he was thin as a reed.
But starving the body did not free the mind.
So he accepted a bowl of rice milk from a village girl, and chose the middle path.
He sat beneath a great fig tree, and vowed not to rise until he understood.
Mara, lord of illusion, sent storms, and armies, and fear. He simply touched the earth.
lines.say: Mahra, lord of illusion, sent storms, and armies, and fear. He simply touched the earth.

lines.text: And as the morning star rose, he awoke. He was the Buddha, the awakened one.
lines.say: And as the morning star rose, he awoke. He was the Boodha, the awakened one.

lines.text: For forty five years he walked from village to village, teaching kindness, and a calm mind.
In many traditions, he is honoured as the ninth avatar of Vishnu,
a reminder that peace is not found in palaces, but within.
